approachQuestion.prompt:
Route Cards. Return one array of node values for every root-to-leaf path of a binary tree, visiting left-child paths before right-child paths. Each returned array must be an independent snapshot. Values include both endpoints. An empty tree returns an empty outer array.

In examples, x(left,right) denotes a node labelled x, and - denotes an absent child. Example 1: Input: 2(4(-,-),7(1(-,-),-)). Output: [[2,4],[2,7,1]]. Example 2: Input: 3(-,-). Output: [[3]]. Example 3: Input: -. Output: [].

Constraints: 0 <= n <= 2000; values are signed 32-bit integers, possibly repeated. The immutable tree has child pointers only, no cycles or shared nodes, and arbitrary shape. Let L be the total number of integer entries in the returned inner arrays; all required output fits memory. Result arrays cannot alias a mutable working path.

options.text: Use explicit enter/exit depth-first frames and one mutable path buffer. Append on entry, copy that buffer into a new result array only at a leaf, and remove the final entry on exit.
options.feedback: The buffer matches the current ancestor path, and leaf-only copies produce independent snapshots in the required order.

options.text: At every descent copy the whole current path for the child. Keep those private copies until their frames finish and return copies at leaves.
options.feedback: The snapshots and order are correct. Intermediate path copies are removable: one enter/exit buffer suffices before copying only the final leaf paths.

options.text: Use one mutable path buffer but append that buffer object itself to the result at every leaf, then remove entries on exit.
options.feedback: Earlier results change when the buffer changes. Example 1 requires two different snapshots, but aliased entries refer to the same ultimately emptied buffer.

options.text: Copy the current root-to-node path into the result at every node, including nodes with children.
options.feedback: Example 1 would include [2] and [2,7], which do not end at leaves and are not requested.

feedback.reason: Separate traversal workspace from unavoidable path-output copying; returning paths has output-sensitive time.
details: Use enter/exit frames in left-first depth-first order. On entry append the node value to one working path. At a leaf allocate an independent array and copy the current path into it, then append that array to the output. On exit remove the node value. Release frames after exit; retain no other paths.

One working path is extended on entry and shortened on exit. Copy it at each leaf so later backtracking cannot mutate an already returned route. Output-sensitive time must include the total copied path length L.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed shared-buffer method for n>=1 nodes and height h in nodes. Let L be the sum of lengths of all returned path arrays. What is the tight total-time and peak auxiliary-space pair? Count the mutable path buffer and explicit frames. Exclude all final output arrays and input. Copying a leaf path of length d costs O(d) time; output construction time is included. Buffer and output-list append are amortized constant-time; shrinking the working path is constant-time.
constraints: All legal shapes are allowed; do not assume balance. Heights count nodes, not edges.

All integer/pointer operations and fixed-size frame operations take constant time. Appending to a dynamic path buffer or output list has amortized constant cost; copying d integers costs O(d). No hashing is used. Count explicit frames and buffer capacity, whose growth retains only a constant multiple of its peak length.

feedback.reason: Traversal events cost n; independent returned route copies add L work.
details: Node entry/exit events cost O(n); all required output copying costs O(L). Live frames and the one mutable path use O(h) space; returned arrays are excluded.
Entry/exit events keep the buffer equal to the current root path. Copying exactly at leaves creates one independent required array per route; processing left before right fixes their order.
“O(n) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Output copies cannot be omitted from time: L can grow faster than n when many leaves share long prefixes.
“O(n+L) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Node entry/exit events cost O(n); all required output copying costs O(L). Live frames and the one mutable path use O(h) space; returned arrays are excluded.
“O(n+L) time, O(L) auxiliary space”: L counts returned entries, which the question excludes from auxiliary space. They are not an additional set of working copies.
“O(nh) time, O(nh) auxiliary space”: This describes unnecessary repeated path storage, not the one-buffer method. Its workspace is bounded by the active path and frames.
